clue.text: Shifting responsibility by handing over the money

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for making someone else take the blame or the decision
second meaning, read literally: a buck is slang for a dollar, so this is giving cash to someone

explanation.surface: Someone dodges blame by paying another person off.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCK is American slang for a dollar; the idiom actually comes from a marker passed round a poker table.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes evading a duty by placing it on another person, and literally means giving a dollar away.

clue.text: Moses' or John's works seen here?

definitions.text: Moses' or John's works seen here?

blocks.note: surface reading: the writings of Moses (the Pentateuch) or John (the Gospel), seen in a Bible

blocks.clueFragment: Moses' or John's works seen here?
blocks.note: setter's reading: Grandma Moses and Augustus John were painters, and their paintings hang where art is displayed

explanation.walkthrough: The names suggest biblical books, but Grandma Moses was an American folk painter and Augustus John a Welsh portraitist.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or room where paintings are exhibited is where you would view works by those two artists.

clue.text: This porcelain's a "must", as seen abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters wander from their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recommendation that this foreign porcelain is essential viewing for travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: Satsuma is a Japanese province famous for its ware; most solvers think of the small orange first.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsuma ware is a cream-coloured Japanese pottery decorated with gilt and enamel, named after its province of origin.

clue.text: At home Henry needs a peak gas supplier

blocks.note: in means at home
Hal is a short form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man called Henry, at home, requires a top-quality gas delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler device delivers medicinal vapour or oxygen for breathing in, so it provides gas to the user.

clue.text: Beast knocking top off tree in clumsy act

indicators.note: knocking off the top removes the first letter of the following word
in places what remains inside the word that comes after

blocks.note: a fir is a conifer tree
a gaffe is a blunder

explanation.surface: An animal clumsily brings down the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The beheaded tree sits just after the first letter of the blunder, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe is a long-necked African mammal, and beast is a general word for any animal.

clue.text: Minor difficulties, but High School captures one t-trophy

indicators.note: to capture is to take inside, so one set of letters encloses the rest

blocks.note: HS is the abbreviation for high school
I is the Roman numeral for one
a trophy is a cup, and the stammer in the clue says to stutter its first letter

explanation.surface: A school's sports team wins a trophy, despite some small setbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer on the t of trophy tells you to stammer the word it gives, CUP, as C-CUP; a hiccup interrupts speech this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiccups are informally small setbacks or glitches, a figurative use of the involuntary spasm.

clue.text: A second science room erected in wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting something stands it on end, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
a lab is a laboratory

explanation.surface: A second laboratory is put up in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very lightweight timber from a tropical American tree, popular for model making.

clue.text: Hint about one fault in the cooking

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps around the others

blocks.note: a cue is a prompt or hint
I is the Roman numeral for one
a sin is a moral failing

explanation.surface: A suggestion about one flaw in the food being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of food preparation, so it can stand in for the cooking of a region or restaurant.

clue.text: Deep matter idly represented, but in a planned way

indicators.note: something represented is presented anew in another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A profound subject presented lazily, yet carefully prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with forethought, deliberately thought out beforehand, as in a crime committed with intent.

clue.text: Salinger's baseball player?

blocks.note: first meaning: the title figure of J D Salinger's best-known novel, The ___ in the Rye
second meaning: the fielder who crouches behind home plate receiving pitches

explanation.walkthrough: Salinger's novel title supplies the word, and in baseball that same word is the fielder who crouches behind the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball this is the defensive player who receives pitches behind home plate, and the word titles Salinger's famous novel.

clue.text: Dog - right one for working underground

blocks.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A dog that is well suited to going down holes in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner works below ground at the coalface, so he is someone employed underground.

clue.text: Informal exchange of calcium for university stock

indicators.note: an exchange swaps one thing out for another, so one element of a word is traded for a replacement

blocks.note: casual means relaxed or informal
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium, the part swapped out
the single-letter abbreviation for university, the part swapped in

explanation.surface: A relaxed trade in which a university gets calcium in return for its goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CASUAL, remove CA and put U in its place to get USUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock reply is a standard, routine one, the kind that is customary and expected.

clue.text: Reworked sum and failed in the old system

indicators.note: something reworked has been redone in a new form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sum was redone and got wrong under the old method of calculation.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval Europe's hierarchy of lords, vassals and serfs holding land in return for service is a historical social order.

clue.text: The precision of former bit of play on water

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an act is a section of a play
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A precise staging of an old scene from a play set on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Water here is a specific body of water: Loch Ness in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness and precision are synonyms, both meaning accuracy without error or deviation.

clue.text: Trusty horse set out with English duke

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A loyal horse heads off, carrying an English duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Steed is a literary or poetic word for a horse, especially one ridden in battle or adventure.

clue.text: Communal fund for a night on the tiles?

blocks.note: first meaning: a savings club whose members pay in weekly, once common in British working-class communities
second meaning, whimsically: roofs are covered with slates, so a club out partying on the roof

explanation.walkthrough: A night on the tiles is British slang for a night out partying; the clue pretends the savings club is a nightclub on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A British savings society where members contribute small sums regularly, often paid out at Christmas, is this kind of pooled fund.

clue.text: The tool to put back part of fireguard

indicators.note: part of tells us only a portion of the following word is wanted, lying inside it
putting something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the letters sitting in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: An instruction to return a tool to its place beside the fire screen.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a boring implement with a helical shaft, used to drill holes in wood or earth.

clue.text: The chap's run out with exercises used with canvas

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing the answer rather than a noun

blocks.note: a guy is a man or chap
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A man has been run out after doing exercises in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: Run out is a way a batsman is dismissed in cricket, abbreviated RO on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent's guy rope is a cord pegged to the ground to hold the canvas taut and steady.

clue.text: State capital's endless ceremony

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: Sacramento is the capital of California

explanation.surface: An unending official ritual held in a state's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a Christian religious rite such as baptism or communion, a solemn ritual observance.

clue.text: Stay upright in a sub?

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: to remain standing inside something
second meaning: a substitute or replacement person

explanation.walkthrough: The sub looks like a submarine where you might stand up; it is a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute who takes someone's place, and standing in somewhere is staying upright inside it.

clue.text: Cry out about a poor act?

definitions.text: Cry out about a poor act?

blocks.clueFragment: Cry out about a poor act?
blocks.note: surface reading: shouting a complaint concerning a bad performance
setter's reading: a cry is literally a noise such as a cat might make, a jeering whistle at a bad performer

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the hint of a cat crying out, since the jeer is named after that animal's yowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a shrill whistle or shout of disapproval directed at a disappointing performer on stage.

clue.text: Mope about, requiring atmosphere to lift in the stores

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are turned into a new order
in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
air means atmosphere

explanation.surface: Someone sulks around the shops, needing fresh air to cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is the Latin plural of emporium, a large shop or trading centre, so stores fits.

clue.text: Wily Tania somehow got ready to attack

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unspecified way, so they need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cunning woman named Tania prepared to pounce.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY is the past tense of lie, so the phrase is past tense like got ready.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide in ambush, concealed and prepared to spring on a victim.

clue.text: Well-known and set to music

blocks.note: first meaning: famous or celebrated
second meaning: written out in musical notation

explanation.surface: A famous lyric that has been given a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A noted person is famous, and a melody that has been notated is written down in musical symbols.

clue.text: One settling abroad to live is put out by personal assistant

indicators.note: putting the word is out ejects those two letters from the previous word
by here means alongside, with the assistant placed within what remains

blocks.note: to exist is to live
PA is the standard abbreviation for personal assistant

explanation.surface: An emigrant aide is annoyed by their personal assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Is put out reads as annoyed, but it tells you to throw the word is out of the verb before adding the assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is a person who has left their native country to make a home in another.

clue.text: Settled down with society in established surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings encircle something, so one piece goes inside the other here

blocks.note: rooted means firmly established
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone settled into familiar company in a well-established setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they settle for the night on a perch, hence perched or came to rest.

clue.text: Tempted everyone headlessly pickled

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is dropped from the following word

blocks.note: all means everyone
cured meat or fish has been pickled or preserved

explanation.surface: Everyone was tempted, having all got drunk to the point of losing their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickled is slang for drunk on the surface, but here it means preserved, CURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to entice or attract, so allured is a synonym for tempted or lured.

clue.text: Scheme to return works here to be shelved?

definitions.text: Scheme to return works here to be shelved?

blocks.clueFragment: Scheme to return works here to be shelved?
blocks.note: surface reading: a plan where finished projects are brought back and abandoned
setter's reading: books borrowed are returned here and put back on shelves

explanation.walkthrough: Shelved usually means postponed; here works are books literally put back on shelves after borrowers return them.
explanation.definitionFit: A library that loans books out operates on the principle that borrowers bring the volumes back.
